The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama model ecosystem.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is introducing new limitations on 'full disk access' for Macs.
The change is a direct response to security risks posed by increasingly capable AI agents.
The new controls aim to ensure users deliberately grant this high level of application access.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A tech CEO was arrested for allegedly smuggling $300M worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent issues regarding the export control and illicit trade of advanced AI hardware.
The story signals continued regulatory and enforcement challenges for major semiconductor companies like Nvidia.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to the broader transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon devices.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: An OpenAI safety employee, David Robinson, has resigned from the company.
Robinson previously authored the safety reports accompanying major OpenAI model releases.
He is now publicly raising concerns about the safety and risks associated with OpenAI's AI models.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has open-sourced the code for its Muse AI agent.
This allows developers to create custom 'Muse gadgets' using the AI.
Suggested applications include displaying reminders on E Ink screens or using it on large HDMI displays.

stories.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Apple is modifying full-disk access permissions to restrict potential misuse by AI agents.
The change addresses concerns regarding AI agents reading private user messages.
The article highlights a disagreement between Apple and Meta regarding the sufficiency of existing regulatory frameworks (like the FDA) to prevent this abuse.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of real-time animation in 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Introduces GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex animations using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much faster, shallow coefficient predictor for efficient avatar animation.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations by moving beyond knowledge-based or high-level agentic tasks to focus on precise CLI command generation.
Features 'runtime-free verifiable rewards,' suggesting a novel method for accurately assessing command correctness without needing full execution environments.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous self-improvement of robot execution systems.
Allows robots to improve capabilities without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
The framework uses offline datasets to identify skills and constructs simulation tasks for practice using execution feedback.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of real-time animation for 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically require costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex avatar animations.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a lightweight, shallow coefficient predictor based on linear combinations of blendshapes.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
It introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool to probe the underlying mathematical capabilities of LLMs.
The findings aim to systematically diagnose current LLM limitations and guide future post-training improvements for better mathematical reasoning.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations by moving beyond knowledge-based tests to measure practical, syntax-sensitive tool invocation capabilities.
Features 'runtime-free verifiable rewards,' suggesting a novel method for accurately assessing command correctness without needing full execution environments.

stories.title: Your coding agent just read your API keys. I built a local check so they don't reach the model.
stories.author: projectescape
bullet_points: Highlights a critical security vulnerability where coding agents might expose sensitive API keys.
Proposes a local solution to prevent confidential credentials from being sent to external models (like OpenAI).
Addresses a growing concern regarding data privacy and security in the rapidly evolving AI coding assistant landscape.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It strengthens Ollama's MLX engine specifically for optimized performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Capcom is actively exploring the integration of AI into game development workflows.
A programmer presented on the 'REX Project' at the Capcom Open Conference, indicating ongoing engine evolution.
The news signals a broader industry trend toward collaborative human-AI game creation, despite potential narrative themes of AI horror.

stories.title: Netflix is pivoting away from prestige
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly shifting its content strategy away from high-prestige, director-driven productions.
The streamer has recently ended multiyear production deals with notable directors, signaling a strategic pivot.
This shift is being analyzed as a potential response or competitive move against rivals.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.author: Allison Johnson
bullet_points: OpenAI has unveiled a new agent platform named Dots.
The platform is positioned as enterprise software, capable of performing tasks ranging from work-related duties to personal actions like ordering food.
The article contrasts Dots with competitors like Meta Muse, noting Dots' more 'workplace software' feel.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon is facing criticism despite taking steps to address data center concerns.
The company received praise for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
The backlash centers on Amazon allegedly downplaying the environmental impact of its data centers.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has reached a settlement of $272.5 million regarding a major driver misclassification lawsuit.
The lawsuit addresses the classification of gig economy workers, a significant labor and tech industry issue.
Critics argue that the settlement amount does not fully compensate the workers involved.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test an AI's ability to find inspiring prior research.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge, where researchers annotate which past papers influenced their current work.
This addresses a key gap in AI research: the ability to sense which buried prior ideas are relevant for novel problem-solving.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The core innovation aims to improve topological preservation and reduce generation costs in complex 3D shape synthesis.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to enhance reasoning capabilities in multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision by allowing direct environmental perception.
The system features a lossless visual memory, enabling the model to actively retrieve and utilize past visual observations.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent sampling bottleneck present in discrete diffusion models during parallel decoding.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state to maintain statistical dependencies among tokens.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) is a new technique for fast visual generation.
It reframes distribution matching as a classification problem to learn log-density ratios directly.
The method aims to improve upon previous distillation techniques by reducing the auxiliary memory and computation costs.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR is designed to explicitly encode complex, higher-order molecular topologies like ring systems and recurring motifs.
The framework aims to overcome the computational demands and decoding difficulties associated with existing higher-order representations.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings instead of fixed class labels or text prompts as conditioning in diffusion transformers.
The method, named Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA), trains a Transformer to predict the next continuous embedding in a sequence.
This approach leverages the sequential nature of image generation, where the clean image's embeddings follow the noisy image's embeddings.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in existing methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) that fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The core innovation is a topology-aware representation designed to improve generation efficiency and structural integrity for complex shapes.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO is a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
It addresses the memory limitations of current LLM fine-tuning by employing a Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse approach.
TACO aims to improve upon existing state compression methods, specifically addressing performance degradation issues seen with alternatives like Muon optimizer.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of finding a generalized Schrödinger bridge on graphs that incorporates a state-visitation cost.
A key finding is that the cost-augmented bridge can be solved exactly by employing a Feynman-Kac tilt on the reference process.
This exact solution eliminates the need for complex learned control mechanisms and temporal-difference penalties previously used in approximation methods.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) are proposed as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent token sampling bottleneck found in discrete diffusion models, which hinders bidirectional reasoning.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, allowing for better capture of inter-token statistical dependencies during parallel decoding.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale neural network optimization for LLMs.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size tuning.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to retrieve inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages expert knowledge, using researchers to annotate which past works influenced their current projects.
Addresses a key challenge in AI research: helping systems discover relevant, foundational ideas buried in vast academic archives.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models mitigate this by denoising a shared continuous state, aiming to maintain inter-token statistical relationships.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of context management in long-horizon coding agents, where early exploration becomes stale.
Introduces 'AutoCompact,' a method that trains coding agents to intelligently decide when and how to compact context.
This work is relevant to advanced AI agents tackling complex, repository-level software engineering tasks.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: The paper identifies a critical flaw where keyword-matching benchmarks can falsely credit small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
Researchers propose a 'ladder of strict, cheap diagnostics' to accurately assess tool-use capabilities in smaller models.
The study demonstrates this false positive using Spanish security language models, highlighting the limitations of lenient evaluation metrics.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of standard post-training methods (SFT and RL) for enhancing frontier models.
It challenges the conventional view that RL is superior for generalization while SFT suffers from weak generalization and catastrophic forgetting.
The proposed method, 'Finetuning with Sampling,' offers a new approach to leverage off-policy expert data, potentially bridging the gap between SFT and RL benefits.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench is a new evaluation framework designed to test data agents on complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only evaluate query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique uses a privileged version of the model to supervise student models, aiming to enhance reasoning capabilities in MLLMs.
It addresses a gap in current MLLM research, which often limits visual information use to simple crops for fine-grained perception.

stories.title: I got targeted: Trying to get your credentials via a git post-checkout hook
stories.author: frankwiles.com by frankwiles
bullet_points: The article discusses a security vulnerability involving Git post-checkout hooks.
The threat involves attackers attempting to steal user credentials via these hooks.
This highlights a specific, practical security risk within developer workflows.
